Homepage Hierarchy Audit
Screenplay homepage · interaction & hierarchy · 30 Sep 2026

Homepage hierarchy audit

Reviewed apps/homepage on main (after the copy changes in PR #1194) with next build && next start, dark only, at 390, 768, 900, 1023, 1024, 1100, 1180, 1280 and 1440px. This pass covers section rhythm, visual hierarchy, the hero carousel and veil, navigation, breakpoints and motion; copy and pixel nits are in the other threads.

Every mockup is the real page with a small CSS or DOM change applied in the browser, so each one is buildable as shown. 14 findings, ranked by how many visitors see them and how much they cost: 3 high, 5 medium, 6 low. Nothing is ticketed yet.

01

The hero backdrop turns to static on most laptop widths

High1024–1250px

From 1024px up the carousel sits under the text with the dither veil. Until about 1250px the headline fits on one line and runs the full measure, so the veil covers nearly the whole stage. No copy of the page is readable; the backdrop reads as TV static with pink specks. At 1023px the same hero shows a clean carousel, so the effect flips from its best state to its worst at one pixel.

Recommendation

Always break the headline after the comma (Every branch,<br>side by side.) or cap the h1 at about 10ch in site/hero.tsx. The right half of the stage then stays clear of the veil at every width above 1024px, which is what the carousel was designed around.

02

Below 1024px the hero stacks two product pictures

High≤1023px

When the carousel moves under the text it becomes a second, unlabelled figure: two rows of tiny homepages, then Fig. 1 right after. On a phone the hero is 1,250px tall and the first thing past the buttons is a strip of miniature copies of the page you are on, which is hard to read without the veil's context.

Recommendation

Keep one row under the text (hide .hc-track + .hc-track below 1024px in hero-stage.css). The motion stays, the hero loses about 200px, and Fig. 1 arrives while the reader still remembers the headline.

03

Self-hosting sells multiplayer but shows none of it

HighAll widths

The back half of the page (Features, Self-hosting, FAQ, CTA) is about 2,300px of text with no picture. Self-hosting is the one section whose pitch is visual (cursors, avatars, comments pinned to the UI), and its left column is a lede, two mono links and 200px of empty space. The links add a third link style to the page (buttons, plain nav links, mono underlines), and one of them is a raw repo URL.

Recommendation

Give the section a frame excerpt with a pinned comment and a facepile (the Problem section's FrameExcerpt plus a pin), move the three perks under the lede, and make the guide link an outline button like the CTA's. Drop the repo URL; GitHub is already in the header.

04

The copies echo the headline right beside it

Medium≥1280px

The copies in the carousel show the same headline, "Every branch, side by side.", at 30 to 40px in full white. Where the veil's edge cuts through them the letters dissolve into fragments like "ranch, side" next to the real H1. They compete with it and the broken glyphs look like a rendering bug more than parallel versions.

Recommendation

Dim the backdrop to about 45% (.hc-backdrop { opacity: .45 }) and let only the copy an agent is editing come up to full strength. The real headline is then the only bright type in the hero, and the working copy becomes the thing the eye follows.

05

Every section has the same weight, and the CTA doesn't close the page

MediumAll widths

Problem, How it works, Features, Self-hosting and FAQ all use the same magenta eyebrow, 56px heading and 140px of top space. Nothing says which sections carry the story and which are reference. The final CTA uses that same heading, so it reads as a sixth section rather than an ending, and its second button (Read the docs) differs from the hero's (Star on GitHub).

Recommendation

Two tiers: the story sections (Problem, How it works) keep 56px; Features, Self-hosting and FAQ drop to 40px. The CTA heading goes up to about 88px as the bookend to the hero, with the hero's button pair.

06

Header links land 165px below the header

MediumAll widths

The sections carry scroll-mt-20, but the 140px top padding sits inside them. Clicking Features leaves a band of empty space and the previous section's column hairlines poking out under the header.

Recommendation

Offset the padding: scroll-margin-top of about −31px on the anchored sections (or move the id onto the heading block with scroll-mt-28). The eyebrow then lands 48px under the header.

07

Phones get no navigation in the header

Medium<768px

Below 768px the nav links disappear with no menu in their place, and below 640px GitHub goes too. The header is the wordmark and a Download button for a Mac app, so a phone visitor can only reach Docs from the footer.

Recommendation

Keep Docs and GitHub as muted text links beside Download on small screens. A menu sheet would also work, but two links fit and match the current header.

08

Step pictures outgrow their headings at tablet widths

Medium640–1023px

Fit scales the 320px step cards to their column, including up. In the two-column layout they grow to 125%, so the mock dialog title "Create workspaces" is larger than the step heading "Ask for versions" and the mock UI text is larger than the body copy under it.

Recommendation

Cap Fit at scale 1 and center the card in its box (Math.min(1, width / design) in excerpts/fit.tsx).

09

Without and With are captioned differently

LowAll widths

"Without Screenplay" sits inside the terminal box; "With Screenplay" sits below the frame. The two captions don't line up, so the pair reads less like a comparison. Stacked below 1024px, the terminal keeps its 320px minimum height and is mostly empty.

Recommendation

Put both captions under their boxes in the same style and drop the terminal's min-h-80 when stacked. The With side could also show two whole frames instead of one and a clipped third of another, since the point is side by side.

10

Step pictures sit between each title and its explanation

LowAll widths

Each step reads label, title, picture, body. The picture splits the title from the sentence that explains it, and on phones the gap is a whole screen. In the other picture-plus-text blocks on the page (Fig. 1, Problem) the picture comes first.

Recommendation

Put the picture first, then Step N, the title and the body, so each column scans top to bottom as one unit and the pictures line up as a row.

11

Group rules and card titles vary between sections

LowAll widths

Steps and FAQ start with a bright rule, Features and Self-hosting with a dim one. Card titles are 22px in Steps, 20px in Features and FAQ and 17px in Self-hosting. Similar blocks get different weights for no reason the reader can see.

Recommendation

One rule: a list or grid starts with a foreground rule and divides with border rules. One card title size (20px).

12

Phone hero buttons stack at two widths

Low<640px

Download for Mac (205px) and Star on GitHub (153px) wrap onto two lines with ragged right edges.

Recommendation

Make both full width when they wrap.

13

GitHub outranks the other header links

Low≥640px

GitHub is in full foreground white while How it works, Features, Self-hosting and Docs are muted, so a secondary link reads as more important than the page's own navigation.

Recommendation

Mute GitHub like the rest; Download stays the one filled action.

14

Keyboard focus looks different on links and buttons

LowAll widths

Buttons get the selection-magenta outline from buttonClass; nav, footer and FAQ links fall back to the browser's white rounded ring.

Recommendation

Apply the same focus-visible:outline-selection outline to every link.

Checked and fine
  • Reduced motion: the carousel holds still, the caret stops blinking and anchor scrolling turns instant.
  • The carousel and veil pause when the hero is off screen, so scrolling the rest of the page costs nothing.
  • FAQ answers animate open where the browser supports it; the sticky header never covers them.
  • No horizontal scroll at any width tested.
